findings.source_passage: So strongly and metaphysically did I conceive of my situation then, that while earnestly watching his motions, I seemed distinctly to perceive that my own individuality was now merged in a joint stock company of two
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically cited passages in the novel—the 'joint stock company of two' formulation is a textual and interpretive signature for Melville's meditation on individuality, free will, and social entanglement. The draft drops 'distinctly' and 'now,' weakening the precision and immediacy Melville built into the sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'I seemed distinctly to perceive that my own individuality was now merged in a joint stock company of two.'

findings.source_passage: I saw that here was a sort of interregnum in Providence; for its even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'interregnum in Providence' and the accusation that Providence's 'even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice' are interpretively essential—they establish Ishmael's challenge to theodicy, a keystone of the novel's theology. The draft retains only 'a sort of interregnum in Providence' and drops the second clause entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'I saw that here was a sort of interregnum in Providence; for its even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice.'

findings.source_passage: This improvement upon the original usage was introduced by no less a man than Stubb, in order to afford the imperilled harpooneer the strongest possible guarantee for the faithfulness and vigilance of his monkey-rope holder.
findings.source_locator: Footnote / asterisk passage after paragraph ending 'one end of it'
findings.why_it_matters: The footnote is a distinct rhetorical device—Melville's mock-scholarly intrusion—and the dry irony of 'no less a man than Stubb' and 'strongest possible guarantee for faithfulness and vigilance' is signature voice-work. The draft collapses this into a parenthetical aside ('Stubb's improvement, made fast at the other end to my own'), losing the footnote form entirely and the irony of 'faithfulness and vigilance.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the footnote as a footnote or at minimum preserve the ironic phrasing 'introduced by no less a man than Stubb' and 'strongest possible guarantee for faithfulness and vigilance of his monkey-rope holder.'

findings.source_passage: There is some sneaking Temperance Society movement about this business,
findings.Will you look at that kannakin, sir: sme: hen watching the mate's countenance, he added,
findings.source_locator: Stubb's speech to Starbuck, paragraph beginning 'There is some sneaking Temperance Society'
findings.why_it_matters: Stubb's extended theatrical harangue to Starbuck—'had the face,' 'calomel and jalap,' 'Is the steward an apothecary, sir?'—is a voice-defining comic set piece. The draft summarizes it in one clause ('He carried the kannakin to Starbuck, who owned it "poor stuff enough"'), erasing Stubb's register and the comic buildup.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's direct address to Starbuck in at least partial dialogue, preserving 'had the face,' 'calomel and jalap,' and the apothecary joke.

findings.source_passage: "Aye, aye, steward," cried Stubb, "we'll teach you to drug a harpooneer; none of your apothecary's medicine here; you want to poison us, do ye? You have got out insurances on our lives and want to murder us all, and pocket the proceeds, do ye?"
findings.source_locator: Paragraph of Stubb's exchange with Dough-Boy and Starbuck
findings.why_it_matters: The insurance-fraud joke ('got out insurances on our lives') is pure Stubb grotesque comedy and a miniature of the novel's commercial/mortality themes. It is entirely absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'poison us / insurances / murder us all and pocket the proceeds' lines in dialogue.

findings.source_passage: hands him—what? Some hot Cognac? No! hands him, ye gods! hands him a cup of tepid ginger and water!
findings.why_it_matters: The triple 'hands him' with 'ye gods!' is a rhythmically and rhetorically distinctive exclamatory climax; the draft drops 'ye gods!' and the second 'hands him,' muting the comic outrage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'hands him, ye gods! hands him a cup of tepid ginger and water!'

summary: Two high-severity losses (the theodicy clause and the 'joint stock company' precision) plus three medium-severity voice flattenings—primarily Stubb's comic harangue and the dropped footnote form—require regeneration.
